links.outcome: Mapping accuracy of humans with vs without AI assistance versus AI alone
links.effect: Agent-assisted pooled hit rate@1 0.868 vs human-only 0.837 (difference 0.031, 95% CI 0.021-0.042) and Agent-only 0.701; R-precision 0.674 vs 0.632.
links.quote: The Agent-assisted human approach achieved a pooled hit rate@1 of 0.868 (95% CI, 0.860–0.876), outperforming both the Agent-only approach (0.701; 95% CI, 0.682–0.720) and the pooled human-only performance (0.837; 95% CI, 0.828–0.845).

links.outcome: AI performance as used by clinicians in workflow versus standalone model
links.effect: Agent-only hit rate@1 0.701 versus Agent-assisted human 0.868; assisted mapping also cut total time 53.9% (1.57 to 0.72 min per segment).
links.quote: Furthermore, agent-assisted mapping significantly outperformed both human-only and Agent-only approaches at k = 1 for all metrics (all p < 0.001).

links.outcome: AI-only and AI-assisted mapping compared with human-only mapping on the same data
links.effect: Agent-only was below human-only on hit rate@1 (difference -0.135, p<0.001), and not different on R-precision (-0.012, p=0.070). Agent-assisted exceeded human-only.
links.quote: Agent-only performed significantly below pooled human-only in hit rate@1 (difference = − 0.135; 95% CI, − 0.148 to − 0.123; p < 0.001).

links.outcome: Reference standard built by blinded panel with adjudication; limitations on error independence
links.effect: Reference set built by three independent managers plus physician adjudication, blind to condition. Authors note correlated errors could bias measured accuracy upward.
links.quote: Both rounds were conducted blind to the experimental origin of the candidate concepts, and only the consensus reached in the second round was retained as the reference set.

links.effect: Agent-assisted 1,638.9 min versus human-only 3,551.0 min; 53.9% reduction (p < 0.001).
links.quote: The mean total mapping time for 2,261 segments was 1,638.9 min (27.3 h) in the Agent-assisted condition, including 431.1 min of agent processing, versus 3,551.0 min (59.2 h) in the human-only condition, a 53.9% reduction ( p < 0.001) (Table 3 ); per-mapper times were 1,737.1, 1,803.1, and 1,376.4 min (reductions of 51.7%, 53.1%, and 57.0%; all p = 0.004).

links.effect: Agent-assisted hit rate@1 0.868 vs Agent-only 0.701 and human-only 0.837; time fell 53.9%, 1.57 to 0.72 min/segment.
links.quote: In this study, the agent-assisted human strategy achieved a pooled hit rate@1 of 0.868 across 2,261 clinical text segments, outperforming both the Agent-only approach (0.701) and unassisted human mapping (0.837), and reduced mean mapping time by 53.9%, from 1.57 to 0.72 min per segment, including the agent’s own processing.

links.effect: 3,224/4,264 reference concepts (75.6%) appeared in top-20; highest-ranked correct concept was rank 1 in 70.1% of segments.
links.quote: Among the 4,264 reference concepts, 3,224 (75.6%) appeared in the agent’s top-20 candidates; the highest-ranked correct concept appeared at rank 1 in 70.1% of segments, within the top 5 in 87.4%, and within the top 20 in 91.9%.
